returnedRecords.text: The CARES Act (March 2020): The first pandemic relief law: $1,200 payments to most adults, expanded unemployment benefits, and forgivable loans to keep small businesses paying staff. The House agreed to the Senate amendment by voice vote on March 27, 2020, so there is no House roll-call position for an individual member. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one additional selected proposal), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

returnedRecords.text: The American Rescue Plan (March 2021): The second big pandemic package: $1,400 payments, an expanded child tax credit that paid parents monthly for a year, and money for vaccines, schools and state governments. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one additional selected proposal), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

returnedRecords.text: The Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (2021): About $550 billion in new money for roads, bridges, water pipes, rural broadband and the electric grid, spread over five years. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one additional selected proposal), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

returnedRecords.text: The Bipartisan Safer Communities Act (2022): The first major federal gun law in about 30 years — tougher checks for buyers under 21, money for state red-flag programs and school mental health. Still in effect; the under-21 provisions expire in 2032 by the law's own terms. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one additional selected proposal), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

returnedRecords.text: The CHIPS and Science Act (2022): About $52 billion to pay companies to build computer-chip factories in the United States, after the pandemic showed how much depends on chips made elsewhere. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one additional selected proposal), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

returnedRecords.text: The Honoring our PACT Act (2022): Extended VA health care and disability benefits to veterans exposed to burn pits and other toxic hazards, and made the government presume certain illnesses were service-related instead of making each veteran prove it. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one additional selected proposal), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

returnedRecords.text: The Inflation Reduction Act (2022): Let Medicare negotiate the price of some prescription drugs and capped insulin at $35 a month for people on Medicare, alongside tax credits for clean energy, paid for partly by a minimum tax on large corporations. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one additional selected proposal), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

returnedRecords.text: The Respect for Marriage Act (2022): Requires every state to recognize same-sex and interracial marriages performed in other states, so those marriages stay valid even if the Supreme Court changes course. returnedRecords.text: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027 (H R 8800): The yearly military policy bill. It says what the Department of Defense (and the Energy Department's nuclear-weapons programs) may spend money on for the 2027 budget year — which aircraft and ships to buy, how many people serve in the military, pay and health care rules for troops, how the Pentagon buys things, how it works with other countries, and rules for cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-29, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008): Bars members of Congress — and their spouses and dependent children — from buying stock in individual companies, and requires public notice 7 to 14 days before they sell stock they already own. Broad investments like widely held funds are exempt. Breaking the rules brings a fine of at least $2,000 or 10% of the trade (plus any profit made), which can't be paid with campaign money. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-17, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Congressional budget for fiscal year 2027 (H CON RES 113): Congress's budget blueprint for 2027 (with targets through 2036). It doesn't spend money itself — it sets the overall numbers for spending, taxes, and debt, and tells four House committees to write follow-up legislation allowed to increase the deficit by set amounts. That follow-up uses a fast-track process the Senate can't filibuster. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-30, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: War Powers resolution on hostilities against Iran (H CON RES 89): Orders the President to pull U.S. armed forces out of hostilities against Iran unless Congress declares war or votes to authorize the use of military force. It says this doesn't stop the U.S. from defending itself, its forces, its diplomatic buildings, or allies from imminent attack. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-04-27, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act (H R 8884): Lets the Social Security Administration restart pilot programs — paused since 2022 — that test changes to disability benefits meant to help people on disability work more without losing income. Joining a pilot is voluntary, a participant's total income can't go down because of it, and the agency must tell Congress about each pilot 120 days before starting it. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-26, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027 (H.R. 6500): A stop-gap spending bill. It keeps the federal government funded — mostly at last year's levels — until December 11, 2026, or until the regular spending bills pass, whichever comes first, preventing a shutdown when the budget year starts October 1. It makes exceptions for programs like WIC food aid, small-business loans, disaster relief, the Indian Health Service, and wildfire fighting, and extends expiring programs covering agriculture, flood insurance, cybersecurity, transportation, veterans benefits, and housing. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-08-12, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027 (H R 8800): The yearly military policy bill. It says what the Department of Defense (and the Energy Department's nuclear-weapons programs) may spend money on for the 2027 budget year — which aircraft and ships to buy, how many people serve in the military, pay and health care rules for troops, how the Pentagon buys things, how it works with other countries, and rules for cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-29, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008): Bars members of Congress — and their spouses and dependent children — from buying stock in individual companies, and requires public notice 7 to 14 days before they sell stock they already own. Broad investments like widely held funds are exempt. Breaking the rules brings a fine of at least $2,000 or 10% of the trade (plus any profit made), which can't be paid with campaign money. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-17, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Congressional budget for fiscal year 2027 (H CON RES 113): Congress's budget blueprint for 2027 (with targets through 2036). It doesn't spend money itself — it sets the overall numbers for spending, taxes, and debt, and tells four House committees to write follow-up legislation allowed to increase the deficit by set amounts. That follow-up uses a fast-track process the Senate can't filibuster. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-30, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: War Powers resolution on hostilities against Iran (H CON RES 89): Orders the President to pull U.S. armed forces out of hostilities against Iran unless Congress declares war or votes to authorize the use of military force. It says this doesn't stop the U.S. from defending itself, its forces, its diplomatic buildings, or allies from imminent attack. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-04-27, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act (H R 8884): Lets the Social Security Administration restart pilot programs — paused since 2022 — that test changes to disability benefits meant to help people on disability work more without losing income. Joining a pilot is voluntary, a participant's total income can't go down because of it, and the agency must tell Congress about each pilot 120 days before starting it. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-26, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027 (H.R. 6500): A stop-gap spending bill. It keeps the federal government funded — mostly at last year's levels — until December 11, 2026, or until the regular spending bills pass, whichever comes first, preventing a shutdown when the budget year starts October 1. It makes exceptions for programs like WIC food aid, small-business loans, disaster relief, the Indian Health Service, and wildfire fighting, and extends expiring programs covering agriculture, flood insurance, cybersecurity, transportation, veterans benefits, and housing. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-08-12, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027 (H R 8800): The yearly military policy bill. It says what the Department of Defense (and the Energy Department's nuclear-weapons programs) may spend money on for the 2027 budget year — which aircraft and ships to buy, how many people serve in the military, pay and health care rules for troops, how the Pentagon buys things, how it works with other countries, and rules for cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-29, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008): Bars members of Congress — and their spouses and dependent children — from buying stock in individual companies, and requires public notice 7 to 14 days before they sell stock they already own. Broad investments like widely held funds are exempt. Breaking the rules brings a fine of at least $2,000 or 10% of the trade (plus any profit made), which can't be paid with campaign money. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-17, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Congressional budget for fiscal year 2027 (H CON RES 113): Congress's budget blueprint for 2027 (with targets through 2036). It doesn't spend money itself — it sets the overall numbers for spending, taxes, and debt, and tells four House committees to write follow-up legislation allowed to increase the deficit by set amounts. That follow-up uses a fast-track process the Senate can't filibuster. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-30, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: War Powers resolution on hostilities against Iran (H CON RES 89): Orders the President to pull U.S. armed forces out of hostilities against Iran unless Congress declares war or votes to authorize the use of military force. It says this doesn't stop the U.S. from defending itself, its forces, its diplomatic buildings, or allies from imminent attack. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-04-27, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act (H R 8884): Lets the Social Security Administration restart pilot programs — paused since 2022 — that test changes to disability benefits meant to help people on disability work more without losing income. Joining a pilot is voluntary, a participant's total income can't go down because of it, and the agency must tell Congress about each pilot 120 days before starting it. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-26, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027 (H.R. 6500): A stop-gap spending bill. It keeps the federal government funded — mostly at last year's levels — until December 11, 2026, or until the regular spending bills pass, whichever comes first, preventing a shutdown when the budget year starts October 1. It makes exceptions for programs like WIC food aid, small-business loans, disaster relief, the Indian Health Service, and wildfire fighting, and extends expiring programs covering agriculture, flood insurance, cybersecurity, transportation, veterans benefits, and housing. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-08-12, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: The CARES Act (March 2020): The first pandemic relief law: $1,200 payments to most adults, expanded unemployment benefits, and forgivable loans to keep small businesses paying staff. The House agreed to the Senate amendment by voice vote on March 27, 2020, so there is no House roll-call position for an individual member. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one additional selected proposal), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.

returnedRecords.text: The American Rescue Plan (March 2021): The second big pandemic package: $1,400 payments, an expanded child tax credit that paid parents monthly for a year, and money for vaccines, schools and state governments. returnedRecords.text: The Bipartisan Safer Communities Act (2022): The first major federal gun law in about 30 years — tougher checks for buyers under 21, money for state red-flag programs and school mental health. returnedRecords.text: The CARES Act (March 2020): The first pandemic relief law: $1,200 payments to most adults, expanded unemployment benefits, and forgivable loans to keep small businesses paying staff. The House agreed to the Senate amendment by voice vote on March 27, 2020, so there is no House roll-call position for an individual member. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one additional selected proposal), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

returnedRecords.text: The American Rescue Plan (March 2021): The second big pandemic package: $1,400 payments, an expanded child tax credit that paid parents monthly for a year, and money for vaccines, schools and state governments. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one additional selected proposal), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

returnedRecords.text: The Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (2021): About $550 billion in new money for roads, bridges, water pipes, rural broadband and the electric grid, spread over five years. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one additional selected proposal), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

returnedRecords.text: The Bipartisan Safer Communities Act (2022): The first major federal gun law in about 30 years — tougher checks for buyers under 21, money for state red-flag programs and school mental health. Still in effect; the under-21 provisions expire in 2032 by the law's own terms. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one additional selected proposal), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

returnedRecords.text: The CHIPS and Science Act (2022): About $52 billion to pay companies to build computer-chip factories in the United States, after the pandemic showed how much depends on chips made elsewhere. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one additional selected proposal), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

returnedRecords.text: The Honoring our PACT Act (2022): Extended VA health care and disability benefits to veterans exposed to burn pits and other toxic hazards, and made the government presume certain illnesses were service-related instead of making each veteran prove it. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one additional selected proposal), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

returnedRecords.text: The Inflation Reduction Act (2022): Let Medicare negotiate the price of some prescription drugs and capped insulin at $35 a month for people on Medicare, alongside tax credits for clean energy, paid for partly by a minimum tax on large corporations. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one additional selected proposal), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

returnedRecords.text: The Respect for Marriage Act (2022): Requires every state to recognize same-sex and interracial marriages performed in other states, so those marriages stay valid even if the Supreme Court changes course. returnedRecords.text: The CARES Act (March 2020): The first pandemic relief law: $1,200 payments to most adults, expanded unemployment benefits, and forgivable loans to keep small businesses paying staff. The House agreed to the Senate amendment by voice vote on March 27, 2020, so there is no House roll-call position for an individual member. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one additional selected proposal), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.

returnedRecords.text: The American Rescue Plan (March 2021): The second big pandemic package: $1,400 payments, an expanded child tax credit that paid parents monthly for a year, and money for vaccines, schools and state governments. returnedRecords.text: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027 (H R 8800): The yearly military policy bill. It says what the Department of Defense (and the Energy Department's nuclear-weapons programs) may spend money on for the 2027 budget year — which aircraft and ships to buy, how many people serve in the military, pay and health care rules for troops, how the Pentagon buys things, how it works with other countries, and rules for cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-29, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008): Bars members of Congress — and their spouses and dependent children — from buying stock in individual companies, and requires public notice 7 to 14 days before they sell stock they already own. Broad investments like widely held funds are exempt. Breaking the rules brings a fine of at least $2,000 or 10% of the trade (plus any profit made), which can't be paid with campaign money. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-17, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Congressional budget for fiscal year 2027 (H CON RES 113): Congress's budget blueprint for 2027 (with targets through 2036). It doesn't spend money itself — it sets the overall numbers for spending, taxes, and debt, and tells four House committees to write follow-up legislation allowed to increase the deficit by set amounts. That follow-up uses a fast-track process the Senate can't filibuster. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-30, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: War Powers resolution on hostilities against Iran (H CON RES 89): Orders the President to pull U.S. armed forces out of hostilities against Iran unless Congress declares war or votes to authorize the use of military force. It says this doesn't stop the U.S. from defending itself, its forces, its diplomatic buildings, or allies from imminent attack. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-04-27, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act (H R 8884): Lets the Social Security Administration restart pilot programs — paused since 2022 — that test changes to disability benefits meant to help people on disability work more without losing income. Joining a pilot is voluntary, a participant's total income can't go down because of it, and the agency must tell Congress about each pilot 120 days before starting it. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-26, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027 (H.R. 6500): A stop-gap spending bill. It keeps the federal government funded — mostly at last year's levels — until December 11, 2026, or until the regular spending bills pass, whichever comes first, preventing a shutdown when the budget year starts October 1. It makes exceptions for programs like WIC food aid, small-business loans, disaster relief, the Indian Health Service, and wildfire fighting, and extends expiring programs covering agriculture, flood insurance, cybersecurity, transportation, veterans benefits, and housing. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-08-12, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027 (H R 8800): The yearly military policy bill. It says what the Department of Defense (and the Energy Department's nuclear-weapons programs) may spend money on for the 2027 budget year — which aircraft and ships to buy, how many people serve in the military, pay and health care rules for troops, how the Pentagon buys things, how it works with other countries, and rules for cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-29, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008): Bars members of Congress — and their spouses and dependent children — from buying stock in individual companies, and requires public notice 7 to 14 days before they sell stock they already own. Broad investments like widely held funds are exempt. Breaking the rules brings a fine of at least $2,000 or 10% of the trade (plus any profit made), which can't be paid with campaign money. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-17, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Congressional budget for fiscal year 2027 (H CON RES 113): Congress's budget blueprint for 2027 (with targets through 2036). It doesn't spend money itself — it sets the overall numbers for spending, taxes, and debt, and tells four House committees to write follow-up legislation allowed to increase the deficit by set amounts. That follow-up uses a fast-track process the Senate can't filibuster. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-30, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: War Powers resolution on hostilities against Iran (H CON RES 89): Orders the President to pull U.S. armed forces out of hostilities against Iran unless Congress declares war or votes to authorize the use of military force. It says this doesn't stop the U.S. from defending itself, its forces, its diplomatic buildings, or allies from imminent attack. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-04-27, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act (H R 8884): Lets the Social Security Administration restart pilot programs — paused since 2022 — that test changes to disability benefits meant to help people on disability work more without losing income. Joining a pilot is voluntary, a participant's total income can't go down because of it, and the agency must tell Congress about each pilot 120 days before starting it. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-26, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027 (H.R. 6500): A stop-gap spending bill. It keeps the federal government funded — mostly at last year's levels — until December 11, 2026, or until the regular spending bills pass, whichever comes first, preventing a shutdown when the budget year starts October 1. It makes exceptions for programs like WIC food aid, small-business loans, disaster relief, the Indian Health Service, and wildfire fighting, and extends expiring programs covering agriculture, flood insurance, cybersecurity, transportation, veterans benefits, and housing. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-08-12, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027 (H R 8800): The yearly military policy bill. It says what the Department of Defense (and the Energy Department's nuclear-weapons programs) may spend money on for the 2027 budget year — which aircraft and ships to buy, how many people serve in the military, pay and health care rules for troops, how the Pentagon buys things, how it works with other countries, and rules for cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-29, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008): Bars members of Congress — and their spouses and dependent children — from buying stock in individual companies, and requires public notice 7 to 14 days before they sell stock they already own. Broad investments like widely held funds are exempt. Breaking the rules brings a fine of at least $2,000 or 10% of the trade (plus any profit made), which can't be paid with campaign money. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-17, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Congressional budget for fiscal year 2027 (H CON RES 113): Congress's budget blueprint for 2027 (with targets through 2036). It doesn't spend money itself — it sets the overall numbers for spending, taxes, and debt, and tells four House committees to write follow-up legislation allowed to increase the deficit by set amounts. That follow-up uses a fast-track process the Senate can't filibuster. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-30, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: War Powers resolution on hostilities against Iran (H CON RES 89): Orders the President to pull U.S. armed forces out of hostilities against Iran unless Congress declares war or votes to authorize the use of military force. It says this doesn't stop the U.S. from defending itself, its forces, its diplomatic buildings, or allies from imminent attack. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-04-27, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act (H R 8884): Lets the Social Security Administration restart pilot programs — paused since 2022 — that test changes to disability benefits meant to help people on disability work more without losing income. Joining a pilot is voluntary, a participant's total income can't go down because of it, and the agency must tell Congress about each pilot 120 days before starting it. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-26, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027 (H.R. 6500): A stop-gap spending bill. It keeps the federal government funded — mostly at last year's levels — until December 11, 2026, or until the regular spending bills pass, whichever comes first, preventing a shutdown when the budget year starts October 1. It makes exceptions for programs like WIC food aid, small-business loans, disaster relief, the Indian Health Service, and wildfire fighting, and extends expiring programs covering agriculture, flood insurance, cybersecurity, transportation, veterans benefits, and housing. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-08-12, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: The CARES Act (March 2020): The first pandemic relief law: $1,200 payments to most adults, expanded unemployment benefits, and forgivable loans to keep small businesses paying staff. The House agreed to the Senate amendment by voice vote on March 27, 2020, so there is no House roll-call position for an individual member. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one additional selected proposal), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.

returnedRecords.text: The American Rescue Plan (March 2021): The second big pandemic package: $1,400 payments, an expanded child tax credit that paid parents monthly for a year, and money for vaccines, schools and state governments. returnedRecords.text: The Bipartisan Safer Communities Act (2022): The first major federal gun law in about 30 years — tougher checks for buyers under 21, money for state red-flag programs and school mental health. returnedRecords.text: The CARES Act (March 2020): The first pandemic relief law: $1,200 payments to most adults, expanded unemployment benefits, and forgivable loans to keep small businesses paying staff. The House agreed to the Senate amendment by voice vote on March 27, 2020, so there is no House roll-call position for an individual member. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one additional selected proposal), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.

returnedRecords.text: The American Rescue Plan (March 2021): The second big pandemic package: $1,400 payments, an expanded child tax credit that paid parents monthly for a year, and money for vaccines, schools and state governments. returnedRecords.text: The Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (2021): About $550 billion in new money for roads, bridges, water pipes, rural broadband and the electric grid, spread over five years. returnedRecords.text: The Bipartisan Safer Communities Act (2022): The first major federal gun law in about 30 years — tougher checks for buyers under 21, money for state red-flag programs and school mental health. returnedRecords.text: The CARES Act (March 2020): The first pandemic relief law: $1,200 payments to most adults, expanded unemployment benefits, and forgivable loans to keep small businesses paying staff. The House agreed to the Senate amendment by voice vote on March 27, 2020, so there is no House roll-call position for an individual member. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one additional selected proposal), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.

returnedRecords.text: The American Rescue Plan (March 2021): The second big pandemic package: $1,400 payments, an expanded child tax credit that paid parents monthly for a year, and money for vaccines, schools and state governments. returnedRecords.text: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027 (H R 8800): The yearly military policy bill. It says what the Department of Defense (and the Energy Department's nuclear-weapons programs) may spend money on for the 2027 budget year — which aircraft and ships to buy, how many people serve in the military, pay and health care rules for troops, how the Pentagon buys things, how it works with other countries, and rules for cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-29, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008): Bars members of Congress — and their spouses and dependent children — from buying stock in individual companies, and requires public notice 7 to 14 days before they sell stock they already own. Broad investments like widely held funds are exempt. Breaking the rules brings a fine of at least $2,000 or 10% of the trade (plus any profit made), which can't be paid with campaign money. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-17, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Congressional budget for fiscal year 2027 (H CON RES 113): Congress's budget blueprint for 2027 (with targets through 2036). It doesn't spend money itself — it sets the overall numbers for spending, taxes, and debt, and tells four House committees to write follow-up legislation allowed to increase the deficit by set amounts. That follow-up uses a fast-track process the Senate can't filibuster. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-30, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: War Powers resolution on hostilities against Iran (H CON RES 89): Orders the President to pull U.S. armed forces out of hostilities against Iran unless Congress declares war or votes to authorize the use of military force. It says this doesn't stop the U.S. from defending itself, its forces, its diplomatic buildings, or allies from imminent attack. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-04-27, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act (H R 8884): Lets the Social Security Administration restart pilot programs — paused since 2022 — that test changes to disability benefits meant to help people on disability work more without losing income. Joining a pilot is voluntary, a participant's total income can't go down because of it, and the agency must tell Congress about each pilot 120 days before starting it. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-26, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027 (H.R. 6500): A stop-gap spending bill. It keeps the federal government funded — mostly at last year's levels — until December 11, 2026, or until the regular spending bills pass, whichever comes first, preventing a shutdown when the budget year starts October 1. It makes exceptions for programs like WIC food aid, small-business loans, disaster relief, the Indian Health Service, and wildfire fighting, and extends expiring programs covering agriculture, flood insurance, cybersecurity, transportation, veterans benefits, and housing. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-08-12, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027 (H R 8800): The yearly military policy bill. It says what the Department of Defense (and the Energy Department's nuclear-weapons programs) may spend money on for the 2027 budget year — which aircraft and ships to buy, how many people serve in the military, pay and health care rules for troops, how the Pentagon buys things, how it works with other countries, and rules for cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-29, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008): Bars members of Congress — and their spouses and dependent children — from buying stock in individual companies, and requires public notice 7 to 14 days before they sell stock they already own. Broad investments like widely held funds are exempt. Breaking the rules brings a fine of at least $2,000 or 10% of the trade (plus any profit made), which can't be paid with campaign money. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-17, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Congressional budget for fiscal year 2027 (H CON RES 113): Congress's budget blueprint for 2027 (with targets through 2036). It doesn't spend money itself — it sets the overall numbers for spending, taxes, and debt, and tells four House committees to write follow-up legislation allowed to increase the deficit by set amounts. That follow-up uses a fast-track process the Senate can't filibuster. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-30, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: War Powers resolution on hostilities against Iran (H CON RES 89): Orders the President to pull U.S. armed forces out of hostilities against Iran unless Congress declares war or votes to authorize the use of military force. It says this doesn't stop the U.S. from defending itself, its forces, its diplomatic buildings, or allies from imminent attack. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-04-27, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act (H R 8884): Lets the Social Security Administration restart pilot programs — paused since 2022 — that test changes to disability benefits meant to help people on disability work more without losing income. Joining a pilot is voluntary, a participant's total income can't go down because of it, and the agency must tell Congress about each pilot 120 days before starting it. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-26, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027 (H.R. 6500): A stop-gap spending bill. It keeps the federal government funded — mostly at last year's levels — until December 11, 2026, or until the regular spending bills pass, whichever comes first, preventing a shutdown when the budget year starts October 1. It makes exceptions for programs like WIC food aid, small-business loans, disaster relief, the Indian Health Service, and wildfire fighting, and extends expiring programs covering agriculture, flood insurance, cybersecurity, transportation, veterans benefits, and housing. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-08-12, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027 (H R 8800): The yearly military policy bill. It says what the Department of Defense (and the Energy Department's nuclear-weapons programs) may spend money on for the 2027 budget year — which aircraft and ships to buy, how many people serve in the military, pay and health care rules for troops, how the Pentagon buys things, how it works with other countries, and rules for cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-29, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008): Bars members of Congress — and their spouses and dependent children — from buying stock in individual companies, and requires public notice 7 to 14 days before they sell stock they already own. Broad investments like widely held funds are exempt. Breaking the rules brings a fine of at least $2,000 or 10% of the trade (plus any profit made), which can't be paid with campaign money. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-17, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Congressional budget for fiscal year 2027 (H CON RES 113): Congress's budget blueprint for 2027 (with targets through 2036). It doesn't spend money itself — it sets the overall numbers for spending, taxes, and debt, and tells four House committees to write follow-up legislation allowed to increase the deficit by set amounts. That follow-up uses a fast-track process the Senate can't filibuster. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-30, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: War Powers resolution on hostilities against Iran (H CON RES 89): Orders the President to pull U.S. armed forces out of hostilities against Iran unless Congress declares war or votes to authorize the use of military force. It says this doesn't stop the U.S. from defending itself, its forces, its diplomatic buildings, or allies from imminent attack. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-04-27, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act (H R 8884): Lets the Social Security Administration restart pilot programs — paused since 2022 — that test changes to disability benefits meant to help people on disability work more without losing income. Joining a pilot is voluntary, a participant's total income can't go down because of it, and the agency must tell Congress about each pilot 120 days before starting it. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-26, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027 (H.R. 6500): A stop-gap spending bill. It keeps the federal government funded — mostly at last year's levels — until December 11, 2026, or until the regular spending bills pass, whichever comes first, preventing a shutdown when the budget year starts October 1. It makes exceptions for programs like WIC food aid, small-business loans, disaster relief, the Indian Health Service, and wildfire fighting, and extends expiring programs covering agriculture, flood insurance, cybersecurity, transportation, veterans benefits, and housing. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-08-12, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

Broad investments like widely held funds are exempt. Breaking the rules brings a fine of at least $2,000 or 10% of the trade (plus any profit made), which can't be paid with campaign money. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-17, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Congressional budget for fiscal year 2027 (H CON RES 113): Congress's budget blueprint for 2027 (with targets through 2036). It doesn't spend money itself — it sets the overall numbers for spending, taxes, and debt, and tells four House committees to write follow-up legislation allowed to increase the deficit by set amounts. That follow-up uses a fast-track process the Senate can't filibuster. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-30, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: War Powers resolution on hostilities against Iran (H CON RES 89): Orders the President to pull U.S. armed forces out of hostilities against Iran unless Congress declares war or votes to authorize the use of military force. It says this doesn't stop the U.S. from defending itself, its forces, its diplomatic buildings, or allies from imminent attack. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-04-27, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act (H R 8884): Lets the Social Security Administration restart pilot programs — paused since 2022 — that test changes to disability benefits meant to help people on disability work more without losing income. Joining a pilot is voluntary, a participant's total income can't go down because of it, and the agency must tell Congress about each pilot 120 days before starting it. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-26, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027 (H.R. 6500): A stop-gap spending bill. It keeps the federal government funded — mostly at last year's levels — until December 11, 2026, or until the regular spending bills pass, whichever comes first, preventing a shutdown when the budget year starts October 1. It makes exceptions for programs like WIC food aid, small-business loans, disaster relief, the Indian Health Service, and wildfire fighting, and extends expiring programs covering agriculture, flood insurance, cybersecurity, transportation, veterans benefits, and housing. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-08-12, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: The CARES Act (March 2020): The first pandemic relief law: $1,200 payments to most adults, expanded unemployment benefits, and forgivable loans to keep small businesses paying staff. The House agreed to the Senate amendment by voice vote on March 27, 2020, so there is no House roll-call position for an individual member. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one additional selected proposal), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

returnedRecords.text: The American Rescue Plan (March 2021): The second big pandemic package: $1,400 payments, an expanded child tax credit that paid parents monthly for a year, and money for vaccines, schools and state governments. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one additional selected proposal), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

returnedRecords.text: The Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (2021): About $550 billion in new money for roads, bridges, water pipes, rural broadband and the electric grid, spread over five years. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one additional selected proposal), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

returnedRecords.text: The Bipartisan Safer Communities Act (2022): The first major federal gun law in about 30 years — tougher checks for buyers under 21, money for state red-flag programs and school mental health. Still in effect; the under-21 provisions expire in 2032 by the law's own terms. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one additional selected proposal), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

returnedRecords.text: The CHIPS and Science Act (2022): About $52 billion to pay companies to build computer-chip factories in the United States, after the pandemic showed how much depends on chips made elsewhere. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one additional selected proposal), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

returnedRecords.text: The Honoring our PACT Act (2022): Extended VA health care and disability benefits to veterans exposed to burn pits and other toxic hazards, and made the government presume certain illnesses were service-related instead of making each veteran prove it. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one additional selected proposal), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

returnedRecords.text: The Inflation Reduction Act (2022): Let Medicare negotiate the price of some prescription drugs and capped insulin at $35 a month for people on Medicare, alongside tax credits for clean energy, paid for partly by a minimum tax on large corporations. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one additional selected proposal), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

returnedRecords.text: The Respect for Marriage Act (2022): Requires every state to recognize same-sex and interracial marriages performed in other states, so those marriages stay valid even if the Supreme Court changes course. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one additional selected proposal), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

returnedRecords.text: The Fiscal Responsibility Act (2023): Ended the debt-ceiling standoff by suspending the borrowing limit into 2025, in exchange for caps on federal spending and new work requirements for some food-stamp recipients. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one additional selected proposal), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.

returnedRecords.text: The shutdown and the 2026 appropriations that ended it: Reopened the federal government after the longest shutdown on record and funded it for the rest of the year, restoring back pay to federal workers and resuming paused federal payments. returnedRecords.text: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027 (H R 8800): The yearly military policy bill. It says what the Department of Defense (and the Energy Department's nuclear-weapons programs) may spend money on for the 2027 budget year — which aircraft and ships to buy, how many people serve in the military, pay and health care rules for troops, how the Pentagon buys things, how it works with other countries, and rules for cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-29, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008): Bars members of Congress — and their spouses and dependent children — from buying stock in individual companies, and requires public notice 7 to 14 days before they sell stock they already own. Broad investments like widely held funds are exempt. Breaking the rules brings a fine of at least $2,000 or 10% of the trade (plus any profit made), which can't be paid with campaign money. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-17, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Congressional budget for fiscal year 2027 (H CON RES 113): Congress's budget blueprint for 2027 (with targets through 2036). It doesn't spend money itself — it sets the overall numbers for spending, taxes, and debt, and tells four House committees to write follow-up legislation allowed to increase the deficit by set amounts. That follow-up uses a fast-track process the Senate can't filibuster. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-30, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: War Powers resolution on hostilities against Iran (H CON RES 89): Orders the President to pull U.S. armed forces out of hostilities against Iran unless Congress declares war or votes to authorize the use of military force. It says this doesn't stop the U.S. from defending itself, its forces, its diplomatic buildings, or allies from imminent attack. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-04-27, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act (H R 8884): Lets the Social Security Administration restart pilot programs — paused since 2022 — that test changes to disability benefits meant to help people on disability work more without losing income. Joining a pilot is voluntary, a participant's total income can't go down because of it, and the agency must tell Congress about each pilot 120 days before starting it. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-26, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027 (H.R. 6500): A stop-gap spending bill. It keeps the federal government funded — mostly at last year's levels — until December 11, 2026, or until the regular spending bills pass, whichever comes first, preventing a shutdown when the budget year starts October 1. It makes exceptions for programs like WIC food aid, small-business loans, disaster relief, the Indian Health Service, and wildfire fighting, and extends expiring programs covering agriculture, flood insurance, cybersecurity, transportation, veterans benefits, and housing. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-08-12, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027 (H R 8800): The yearly military policy bill. It says what the Department of Defense (and the Energy Department's nuclear-weapons programs) may spend money on for the 2027 budget year — which aircraft and ships to buy, how many people serve in the military, pay and health care rules for troops, how the Pentagon buys things, how it works with other countries, and rules for cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-29, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008): Bars members of Congress — and their spouses and dependent children — from buying stock in individual companies, and requires public notice 7 to 14 days before they sell stock they already own. Broad investments like widely held funds are exempt. Breaking the rules brings a fine of at least $2,000 or 10% of the trade (plus any profit made), which can't be paid with campaign money. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-17, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Congressional budget for fiscal year 2027 (H CON RES 113): Congress's budget blueprint for 2027 (with targets through 2036). It doesn't spend money itself — it sets the overall numbers for spending, taxes, and debt, and tells four House committees to write follow-up legislation allowed to increase the deficit by set amounts. That follow-up uses a fast-track process the Senate can't filibuster. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-30, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: War Powers resolution on hostilities against Iran (H CON RES 89): Orders the President to pull U.S. armed forces out of hostilities against Iran unless Congress declares war or votes to authorize the use of military force. It says this doesn't stop the U.S. from defending itself, its forces, its diplomatic buildings, or allies from imminent attack. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-04-27, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act (H R 8884): Lets the Social Security Administration restart pilot programs — paused since 2022 — that test changes to disability benefits meant to help people on disability work more without losing income. Joining a pilot is voluntary, a participant's total income can't go down because of it, and the agency must tell Congress about each pilot 120 days before starting it. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-26, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027 (H.R. 6500): A stop-gap spending bill. It keeps the federal government funded — mostly at last year's levels — until December 11, 2026, or until the regular spending bills pass, whichever comes first, preventing a shutdown when the budget year starts October 1. It makes exceptions for programs like WIC food aid, small-business loans, disaster relief, the Indian Health Service, and wildfire fighting, and extends expiring programs covering agriculture, flood insurance, cybersecurity, transportation, veterans benefits, and housing. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-08-12, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027 (H R 8800): The yearly military policy bill. It says what the Department of Defense (and the Energy Department's nuclear-weapons programs) may spend money on for the 2027 budget year — which aircraft and ships to buy, how many people serve in the military, pay and health care rules for troops, how the Pentagon buys things, how it works with other countries, and rules for cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-29, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008): Bars members of Congress — and their spouses and dependent children — from buying stock in individual companies, and requires public notice 7 to 14 days before they sell stock they already own. Broad investments like widely held funds are exempt. Breaking the rules brings a fine of at least $2,000 or 10% of the trade (plus any profit made), which can't be paid with campaign money. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-17, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Congressional budget for fiscal year 2027 (H CON RES 113): Congress's budget blueprint for 2027 (with targets through 2036). It doesn't spend money itself — it sets the overall numbers for spending, taxes, and debt, and tells four House committees to write follow-up legislation allowed to increase the deficit by set amounts. That follow-up uses a fast-track process the Senate can't filibuster. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-30, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: War Powers resolution on hostilities against Iran (H CON RES 89): Orders the President to pull U.S. armed forces out of hostilities against Iran unless Congress declares war or votes to authorize the use of military force. It says this doesn't stop the U.S. from defending itself, its forces, its diplomatic buildings, or allies from imminent attack. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-04-27, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act (H R 8884): Lets the Social Security Administration restart pilot programs — paused since 2022 — that test changes to disability benefits meant to help people on disability work more without losing income. Joining a pilot is voluntary, a participant's total income can't go down because of it, and the agency must tell Congress about each pilot 120 days before starting it. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-26, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027 (H.R. 6500): A stop-gap spending bill. It keeps the federal government funded — mostly at last year's levels — until December 11, 2026, or until the regular spending bills pass, whichever comes first, preventing a shutdown when the budget year starts October 1. It makes exceptions for programs like WIC food aid, small-business loans, disaster relief, the Indian Health Service, and wildfire fighting, and extends expiring programs covering agriculture, flood insurance, cybersecurity, transportation, veterans benefits, and housing. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-08-12, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: The CARES Act (March 2020): The first pandemic relief law: $1,200 payments to most adults, expanded unemployment benefits, and forgivable loans to keep small businesses paying staff. returnedRecords.text: The CARES Act (March 2020): The first pandemic relief law: $1,200 payments to most adults, expanded unemployment benefits, and forgivable loans to keep small businesses paying staff. returnedRecords.text: The CARES Act (March 2020): The first pandemic relief law: $1,200 payments to most adults, expanded unemployment benefits, and forgivable loans to keep small businesses paying staff. The House agreed to the Senate amendment by voice vote on March 27, 2020, so there is no House roll-call position for an individual member. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one additional selected proposal), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.

returnedRecords.text: The American Rescue Plan (March 2021): The second big pandemic package: $1,400 payments, an expanded child tax credit that paid parents monthly for a year, and money for vaccines, schools and state governments. returnedRecords.text: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027 (H R 8800): The yearly military policy bill. It says what the Department of Defense (and the Energy Department's nuclear-weapons programs) may spend money on for the 2027 budget year — which aircraft and ships to buy, how many people serve in the military, pay and health care rules for troops, how the Pentagon buys things, how it works with other countries, and rules for cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-29, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008): Bars members of Congress — and their spouses and dependent children — from buying stock in individual companies, and requires public notice 7 to 14 days before they sell stock they already own. Broad investments like widely held funds are exempt. Breaking the rules brings a fine of at least $2,000 or 10% of the trade (plus any profit made), which can't be paid with campaign money. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-17, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Congressional budget for fiscal year 2027 (H CON RES 113): Congress's budget blueprint for 2027 (with targets through 2036). It doesn't spend money itself — it sets the overall numbers for spending, taxes, and debt, and tells four House committees to write follow-up legislation allowed to increase the deficit by set amounts. That follow-up uses a fast-track process the Senate can't filibuster. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-30, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: War Powers resolution on hostilities against Iran (H CON RES 89): Orders the President to pull U.S. armed forces out of hostilities against Iran unless Congress declares war or votes to authorize the use of military force. It says this doesn't stop the U.S. from defending itself, its forces, its diplomatic buildings, or allies from imminent attack. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-04-27, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act (H R 8884): Lets the Social Security Administration restart pilot programs — paused since 2022 — that test changes to disability benefits meant to help people on disability work more without losing income. Joining a pilot is voluntary, a participant's total income can't go down because of it, and the agency must tell Congress about each pilot 120 days before starting it. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-26, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027 (H.R. 6500): A stop-gap spending bill. It keeps the federal government funded — mostly at last year's levels — until December 11, 2026, or until the regular spending bills pass, whichever comes first, preventing a shutdown when the budget year starts October 1. It makes exceptions for programs like WIC food aid, small-business loans, disaster relief, the Indian Health Service, and wildfire fighting, and extends expiring programs covering agriculture, flood insurance, cybersecurity, transportation, veterans benefits, and housing. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-08-12, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: War Powers resolution on hostilities against Iran (S.J.Res. 181): Orders the President to remove U.S. armed forces from hostilities in or against Iran unless Congress declares war or votes to authorize the use of military force. returnedRecords.text: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027 (H.R. 6500): A stop-gap spending bill. It keeps the federal government funded — mostly at last year's levels — until December 11, 2026, or until the regular spending bills pass, whichever comes first, preventing a shutdown when the budget year starts October 1. It makes exceptions for programs like WIC food aid, small-business loans, disaster relief, the Indian Health Service, and wildfire fighting, and extends expiring programs covering agriculture, flood insurance, cybersecurity, transportation, veterans benefits, and housing. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-08-12, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Photo identification requirements for federal elections (S. 5271): Requires voters to show physical photo ID to get a ballot in federal elections. Someone without ID can cast a provisional ballot, but it only counts if they show ID within three days (or swear they lack it for religious reasons). Voting by mail would require sending a copy of a photo ID, or the last four digits of a Social Security number plus a sworn statement that ID couldn't reasonably be obtained. Overseas military voters and certain disabled or elderly voters are exempt, and states must work to make free ID imaging available. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-08-11, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027 (H R 8800): The yearly military policy bill. It says what the Department of Defense (and the Energy Department's nuclear-weapons programs) may spend money on for the 2027 budget year — which aircraft and ships to buy, how many people serve in the military, pay and health care rules for troops, how the Pentagon buys things, how it works with other countries, and rules for cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-29, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008): Bars members of Congress — and their spouses and dependent children — from buying stock in individual companies, and requires public notice 7 to 14 days before they sell stock they already own. Broad investments like widely held funds are exempt. Breaking the rules brings a fine of at least $2,000 or 10% of the trade (plus any profit made), which can't be paid with campaign money. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-17, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Congressional budget for fiscal year 2027 (H CON RES 113): Congress's budget blueprint for 2027 (with targets through 2036). It doesn't spend money itself — it sets the overall numbers for spending, taxes, and debt, and tells four House committees to write follow-up legislation allowed to increase the deficit by set amounts. That follow-up uses a fast-track process the Senate can't filibuster. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-30, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: War Powers resolution on hostilities against Iran (H CON RES 89): Orders the President to pull U.S. armed forces out of hostilities against Iran unless Congress declares war or votes to authorize the use of military force. It says this doesn't stop the U.S. from defending itself, its forces, its diplomatic buildings, or allies from imminent attack. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-04-27, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act (H R 8884): Lets the Social Security Administration restart pilot programs — paused since 2022 — that test changes to disability benefits meant to help people on disability work more without losing income. Joining a pilot is voluntary, a participant's total income can't go down because of it, and the agency must tell Congress about each pilot 120 days before starting it. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-26, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027 (H.R. 6500): A stop-gap spending bill. It keeps the federal government funded — mostly at last year's levels — until December 11, 2026, or until the regular spending bills pass, whichever comes first, preventing a shutdown when the budget year starts October 1. It makes exceptions for programs like WIC food aid, small-business loans, disaster relief, the Indian Health Service, and wildfire fighting, and extends expiring programs covering agriculture, flood insurance, cybersecurity, transportation, veterans benefits, and housing. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-08-12, read at the bill page.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

returnedRecords.text: War Powers resolution on hostilities against Iran (H CON RES 89): Orders the President to pull U.S. armed forces out of hostilities against Iran unless Congress declares war or votes to authorize the use of military force. It says this doesn't stop the U.S. from defending itself, its forces, its diplomatic buildings, or allies from imminent attack. returnedRecords.text: Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act (H R 8884): Lets the Social Security Administration restart pilot programs — paused since 2022 — that test changes to disability benefits meant to help people on disability work more without losing income. Joining a pilot is voluntary, a participant's total income can't go down because of it, and the agency must tell Congress about each pilot 120 days before starting it. returnedRecords.text: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027 (H.R. 6500): A stop-gap spending bill. It keeps the federal government funded — mostly at last year's levels — until December 11, 2026, or until the regular spending bills pass, whichever comes first, preventing a shutdown when the budget year starts October 1. It makes exceptions for programs like WIC food aid, small-business loans, disaster relief, the Indian Health Service, and wildfire fighting, and extends expiring programs covering agriculture, flood insurance, cybersecurity, transportation, veterans benefits, and housing. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-08-12, read at the bill page.

returnedRecords.text: The CARES Act (March 2020): The first pandemic relief law: $1,200 payments to most adults, expanded unemployment benefits, and forgivable loans to keep small businesses paying staff. The House agreed to the Senate amendment by voice vote on March 27, 2020, so there is no House roll-call position for an individual member. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one additional selected proposal), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

returnedRecords.text: The American Rescue Plan (March 2021): The second big pandemic package: $1,400 payments, an expanded child tax credit that paid parents monthly for a year, and money for vaccines, schools and state governments. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one additional selected proposal), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
returnedRecords.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

returnedRecords.text: The Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (2021): About $550 billion in new money for roads, bridges, water pipes, rural broadband and the electric grid, spread over five years. returnedRecords.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

returnedRecords.text: The Bipartisan Safer Communities Act (2022): The first major federal gun law in about 30 years — tougher checks for buyers under 21, money for state red-flag programs and school mental health. Still in effect; the under-21 provisions expire in 2032 by the law's own terms. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one additional selected proposal), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.

It says what the Department of Defense (and the Energy Department's nuclear-weapons programs) may spend money on for the 2027 budget year — which aircraft and ships to buy, how many people serve in the military, pay and health care rules for troops, how the Pentagon buys things, how it works with other countries, and rules for cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. returnedRecords.text: Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008): Bars members of Congress — and their spouses and dependent children — from buying stock in individual companies, and requires public notice 7 to 14 days before they sell stock they already own. returnedRecords.text: The CARES Act (March 2020): The first pandemic relief law: $1,200 payments to most adults, expanded unemployment benefits, and forgivable loans to keep small businesses paying staff.
